correctness.rationale: Four joint and marginal probabilities follow by explicit partition of all possible outbreak seeds and open paths. Direct subtraction yields both factored covariances. A is strictly increasing and has one root; B is initially decreasing and strictly convex, hence has one interior root for \(k\ge3\), and remains negative for k=2. An exact polynomial inequality orders the roots; rescaling B and bracketing its single root prove \(k^{-2/3}\), while the explicit A root proves \(k^{-1}\). Endpoints and k=1 are handled. The executable independently checks 5,503 exact assertions and 12 numerical diagnostics for finite special cases; the continuous/all-degree statements rely on the analytic argument.

value.rationale: Uniform introduction of one initial case is a natural model of outbreak uncertainty. The complete sign diagram is a structural classification distinguishing hub-leaf from leaf-leaf co-infection, with a finite intermediate regime and provably different large-degree transition scales. These are behaviorally relevant exact correlation benchmarks not determined by expected outbreak size, even though the derivation is self-contained on a star. No empirical or policy claims are made.
